interest: This document is valuable to historians studying Anglo-Japanese and U.S.-Japanese diplomatic relations immediately preceding the outbreak of the Pacific War in 1941. It documents the Japanese Empire's restrictive and discriminatory visa policies toward British subjects across Japanese-controlled areas, as observed and reported by U.S. consular officials in China and Manchuria to the American Embassy at Beijing. In addition, it provides insight into State Department recordkeeping methods, demonstrating how cross-reference docket sheets were maintained for decimal file 894.5541 (immigration from the UK) while linking related reports to passport and visa classification 894.1117.
overview: This file consists of a U.S. Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.5541, titled 'Immigration To Japan From United Kingdom' (recorded on the sheet as 'Visitation to Japan from Great Britain'). The sheet records a single entry dated June 19, 1941, documenting Despatch No. 107 from Harbin (transcribed in the OCR as 'Wachin') drafted by Foreign Service Officer Wurley and addressed to the American Embassy at Beijing on the subject of Japanese restrictive policy in granting visas to British subjects. The entry notes the transmission of a copy to the Department of State in Washington and cross-references the filing under decimal file 894.1117.

subfiles.summary: This single-page document is a State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.5541 concerning immigration and visitation to Japan from Great Britain. It logs Sub No. 1, a despatch dated June 19, 1941, from Harbin (recorded as 'Wachin') drafted by officer Wurley to the American Embassy at Beijing regarding Japanese restrictive policy in granting visas to British subjects. The sheet notes the transmission of a copy to Washington and records a cross-reference to decimal file 894.1117.
